full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioner, Md. Mazibur Rahman Talukdcr, is that he is a bonafide businessman running a printing press at Madaripur Town at holding No. 799, Puranbazar, Madaripur, The petitioner was a tenant in the said holding under respondent Nos. 5, and 6 on monthly rental basis since 1981. He imported the said printing machine from China by taking loan from the Government In month of December, 1988. The petitioner went to his village home keeping the press closed to attend some urgent family matters and met with an accident and became temporarily disabled and took rest at his village home for some time when he was served with a notice (Annexure-A) issued by the respondent No. 1 directing him to appear before him on 28.12.88 for hearing a complaint petition filed by the petitioner's landlords, respondent Nos. 5 and 6, for evicting the petitioner therefrom. The petitioner could not appear but sent an application for time expressing his inability to move. After recovery from the injuries, the petitioner returned to Madaripur by the end of February, 1989 and found the press premises locked under the lock, and key of the landlords replacing the petitioner's lock and key. On inquiry he came to know that during his absence he was evicted and his press and other valuables were taken away by the order of the respondent No. I but he could not get any information as to what happened to his press and machineries, etc. worth about Taka 1,66,000.00 which were inside the said room. He filed an application before the respondent No.1 but without any result. The petitioner filed an application for certified copies of the relevant orders but he was not supplied with the same. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, Superintendent of the office of respondent No. 1, is the brother in-law of Kazi Alauddin Ahmed, respondent No. 5, one of the landlords of the petitioner who managed get all these actions taken by the respondent Nos. 1, and 2. Finally, the petitioner filed an application to the Deputy Commissioner, Madaripur stating all the facts but without any result. He was finally given all unsigned copy of the eviction order and the seizure list prepared by respondent No. 2 (Annexure-F) from the Office Of the respondent No. 1, the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, It is the further case of the petitioner that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 had no jurisdiction to pass such order or to take such action which are without lawful authority. 

 4. It is the further case of the contesting respondents that the rented premises was seriously damaged by the devastating flood of September, 1988 and the house was under lock, and key of the petitioner since first part of February, 1988 and he was also defaulter in respect of payment of rem since January, 1981 so the petitioner was liable to be evicted from the rented premises. The respondent Nos. 5 and 6 terminated the tenancy of the petitioner by serving a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of 'Property Act with the expiry of January 1987. they filed an application before the respondent No. 1 who issued notice to the petitioner on several occasions but he did not appear. The respondent No. l started a Miscellaneous Case No.XIII-6/88-89 on their application. It has not been categorically denied that the Office Superintendent of respondent No. 1 is the brother-in-law of one of the landlords. 

 8. After the notice of termination is served on the tenant if it is not complied with, the proper course of action is to file a suit for eviction in the civil Court, but the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 instead of going to the civil Court approached the respondent No. 1 and the respondent No. 1 usurped the power of the civil Court and started a miscellaneous case. So, the issuance of the impugned notice dated 19.12.88 and all subsequent proceedings and actions taken are without any lawful authority. It appears from Annexure F to the petition that the respondent No. 2 by order of the respondent No. 1 broke the lock of the petitioner and evicted the petitioner in his absence and removed all his materials including the printing machine and other article and kept those in the custody of one Sckander Ali Munshi stated to be the President of the Bazar Committee. This action of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer and the Upazila Magistrate, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 respectively, are nothing but high handedness on the part of the public servants dealing with the public and eviction of a person from his tenanted house and removing of his belongings are all malafide. The possibility of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer's acting at the instance and influence of his Office Superintendent Mr. Mukhlesur Rahman, brother-in-law of Kazi Alauddin Ahmed, respondent No. 5, one of the landlords of the petitioner cannot be overruled. The respondent No.1 went out of the way to evict a tenant of the private individual, This is a glaring instance of misuse of power on the part of responsible officers connected with the administration of Upazila, The respondent Nos. 1 and 2, therefore, are answerable for their unauthorized conduct. They have not filed any affidavit-in-opposition denying the allegations made in the petition or to justify their action. Neither the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Government nor the learned advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 has been able to point out any provision of law authorizing the respondent Nos. 14 or 2 to take the impugned action.
